title: A 15/31 Counterexample Family to the Albertson-Berman Conjecture
summary: For a graph $G$, let $a(G)$ be the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest. The Albertson-Berman conjecture, posed in 1979, asserts that every $n$-vertex planar graph satisfies $a(G)\ge n/2$. Borodin's bound $a(G)\ge 2n/5$ remains the general lower bound toward this problem. We disprove the conjecture with an explicit 31-vertex plane triangulation $T$ satisfying $a(T)=15$. Moreover, for every integer $k\ge2$, we construct a simple planar graph $M_k$ with $|V(M_k)|=31k$ and $a(M_k)=15k$, so that $a(M_k)/|V(M_k)|=15/31<1/2$.
